column1: # AQL Language Specification: the `class` word — sealed nominal records
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# `def Foo class {schema}` defines a class: a sealed nominal record
# type rooted under Ideal/Class (NOT under Object — Object is the open
# mutable keyed container; classes are sealed nominal records — see
# design/CLASS-OBJECT.10.md). Schema entries: a TYPE value declares a
# required field; a CONCRETE value declares a default (the field's
# type is the value's own type). Instances are FLAT (every field, own
# and inherited, resolves eagerly at make — no prototype chain) and
# SEALED (writing an undeclared field is a loud sealed_field error).
# Subclassing reuses refine: `def Bar refine Foo {…}`.
# §1  definition + construction (paren-free def, defaults, dot reads)
def Point class {x:1, y:2} (make Point {}) get x
column3: paren-free def + make; omitted field takes its default

column1: def Point class {x:1, y:2} (make Point {x:9}) get x
column3: provided value overrides the default

column1: def Point class {x:1, y:2} def p (make Point {x:9}) p.y
column3: dot access reads an instance field (literal key)

column1: def Point class {x:1} (make Point {}) typeof
column3: typeof an instance is the class name

column1: def Point class {x:1} (make Point {}) is Point
column3: an instance is its class

column1: def Point class {x:1} (make Point {}) is Object
column3: a class instance is NOT an Object — classes root under Ideal/Class

column1: # §2  required vs defaulted fields (type = required, value = default)
def User class {name:String, age:0} (make User {name:'ann'}) get age
column3: typed field provided, valued field defaults

column1: def User class {name:String, age:0} make User {}
column3: a typed field is REQUIRED — omitting it is a loud error

column1: def Point class {x:1} make Point {z:5}
column3: an undeclared key at make is a loud error

column1: # §3  sealing — set writes declared fields in place, rejects others
def Point class {x:1} def p (make Point {}) p set x 7 end p.x
column3: declared-field set writes in place (returns nothing)

column1: def Point class {x:1} def p (make Point {}) p set z 9
column3: an undeclared field write is a loud sealed_field error

column1: # §4  subclassing via refine — flat inherited defaults, sealed across the chain
def Point class {x:1} def Point3 refine Point {z:3} (make Point3 {}) get x
column3: inherited default resolves flat into the instance

column1: def Point class {x:1} def Point3 refine Point {z:3} (make Point3 {x:7}) get z
column3: own default alongside provided inherited field

column1: def Point class {x:1} def Point3 refine Point {z:3} (make Point3 {}) is Point
column3: an instance of the subclass is the parent class (nominal chain)

column1: def Point class {x:1} def Point3 refine Point {z:3} (make Point3 {}) is Point3
column3: …and is its own class

column1: def Point class {x:1} def Point3 refine Point {z:3} (make Point3 {}) set w 1
column3: sealing covers the whole inherited field set

column1: # §5  errors — malformed definitions
def Bad class 5
column3: the schema must be a map

column1: class Map
column3: a bare Map type literal is not a concrete schema map (matcher refuses it)

column1: # §6  strict field typing — no silent conversion (unlike legacy objects)
def Point class {x:1} make Point {x:'hi'}
column3: a defaulted field rejects values outside the default's own type

column1: def Point class {x:1} make Point {x:2.5}
column3: no silent Float→Integer truncation — loud type error

column1: def User class {name:String} make User {name:42}
column3: a typed field rejects non-conforming values (no conversion)

column1: def Radius (Float gte 0.0) def Circle class {r:Radius} (make Circle {r:2.0}) get r
column3: a predicate-typed field runs its predicate at make and accepts

column1: def Radius (Float gte 0.0) def Circle class {r:Radius} make Circle {r:-1.0}
column3: …and rejects a violating value loudly

column1: def Radius (Float gte 0.0) def Circle class {r:Radius} def c (make Circle {r:1.0}) c set r -5.0
column3: write-time enforcement matches construction (predicate runs at set)

column1: def Radius (Float gte 0.0) def Circle class {r:Radius} def c (make Circle {r:1.0}) c set r 3.0 end c.r
column3: a conforming write succeeds

column1: # §7  instance equality + enumeration
# eq = identity (two bindings to ONE instance); deq = same class AND
# structurally equal fields; cross-class and subclass-vs-parent twins
# are never deq-equal. Enumeration sees the flat field map.
def P class {x:1} (make P {x:5}) (make P {x:5}) deq
column3: deq: same-class structural twins are equal

column1: def P class {x:1} (make P {x:5}) (make P {x:6}) deq
column3: deq: differing field values are not

column1: def P class {x:1} def Q class {x:1} (make P {}) (make Q {}) deq
column3: deq: different classes never compare equal, even with equal fields

column1: def P class {x:1} def P2 refine P {} (make P {}) (make P2 {}) deq
column3: deq: a subclass instance is not deq-equal to a parent instance

column1: def P class {x:1} def a (make P {}) def b a a b eq
column3: eq: two bindings to one instance are identical

column1: def P class {x:1} (make P {}) (make P {}) eq
column3: eq: structural twins are NOT identical (that is deq's job)

column1: def P class {x:1, y:2} (make P {}) size
column3: size: the flat field count

column1: def P class {x:1} convert Map (make P {})
column3: convert Map: the flat field map

column1: aql:struct-util import end  def P class {x:1, y:2} StructUtil.items (make P {y:9})
column3: items: every field enumerates (defaults included)

column1: def P class {x:1} (make P {x:1}) cmp (make P {x:2})
column3: cmp: same-class instances order field-wise

column1: # §8  the removed legacy form + paren-free def
def Box class {v:0} def b make Box {v:9} end b.v
column3: def + make is paren-free — the nested-collection shape, like def name fn […]

column1: def Box (refine Object {v:0})
column3: refine Object is removed — class {…} is the class form (no alias)

column1: refine Object {v:0}
column3: …also without def

column1: # §9  typed defaults via tagged make — `make Foo v` constructs a
#     scalar-refinement value (cast to base, then tagged), so a
#     default constructed at the refined type declares BOTH the field
#     type and the default: {x:(make Foo 1)}.
def Foo refine Integer end (make Foo 1) is Foo
column3: make on a newtype tags the value

column1: def Foo refine Integer end (make Foo 1) typeof
column3: …and typeof shows the refinement

column1: def Foo refine Integer end (make Foo "42") is Foo
column3: make casts to the base first (String → Integer), then tags

column1: def Foo refine Integer end def S class {x:(make Foo 1)} end (typeof ((make S {}) get x))
column3: a tagged default declares the field type AND fills when omitted

column1: def Foo refine Integer end def S class {x:(make Foo 1)} end make S {x:7}
column3: a bare Integer is not a Foo — newtype strictness extends to fields

column1: def Foo refine Integer end def S class {x:(make Foo 1)} end (make S {x:(make Foo 7)}) get x
column3: a properly-tagged value is accepted

column1: # §10  const — singleton types: a field that can only ever hold one value
def S class {kind:(const 'point'), x:1} end (make S {}) get kind
column3: a const member's default is forced — the only inhabitant fills in

column1: def S class {kind:(const 'point'), x:1} end (make S {kind:'point', x:2}) get x
column3: providing the exact inhabitant is accepted

column1: def S class {kind:(const 'point')} end make S {kind:'other'}
column3: any other value is a loud type error at make

column1: def S class {kind:(const 'point')} end def s (make S {}) end s set kind 'other'
column3: …and at instance set

column1: def S class {kind:(const 'point')} end def s (make S {}) end s set kind 'point' end s.kind
column3: re-writing the inhabitant succeeds

column1: typeof (const 1)
column3: the singleton's name renders as its value

column1: def One (typeof (const 1)) end 1 is One
column3: the plain inhabitant is a member

column1: def One (typeof (const 1)) end 2 is One
column3: other values are not

column1: def One (typeof (const 1)) end 1.0 is One
column3: same-base strict — cmp's cross-leaf magnitude equivalence does not leak into membership

column1: def P class {x:1} end const (make P {})
column3: a mutable instance cannot pin a value

column1: const nan
column3: NaN cannot pin a value (not equal to itself)

column1: (typeof (const 1)) teq (typeof (const 1))
column3: const singletons intern — one lattice node per (base, value)

column1: # §11  undef of a class with live instances — undef removes the NAME
#      (make on the old name is a loud undefined_word), but live
#      instances keep their identity: reads, typed writes, and typeof
#      keep working against the retired node.
def Point class {x:1} def p (make Point {x:5}) undef Point end p typeof
column3: a live instance keeps its type identity after undef

column1: def Point class {x:1} def p (make Point {x:5}) undef Point end p get x
column3: …and its fields stay readable

column1: def Point class {x:1} def p (make Point {x:5}) undef Point end p set x 9 end p.x
column3: …and typed writes still run the schema check

column1: def Point class {x:1} def p (make Point {x:5}) undef Point end p set x 'hi'
column3: …which still rejects off-schema values

column1: def Point class {x:1} def p (make Point {}) undef Point end make Point {}
column3: the NAME is gone — construction is a loud error
